description:
FILED s452ab (Opus, round 11 agent AB), seen in the #721 emission A/B.
PRE-EXISTING; #721 changed the WRONG VALUE, not the wrongness.

    use feature 'signatures';
    package T200 { sub foo ($x) {} }   # empty body
    my @r = T200::foo(7);
        perl: 0 elements               (the body is empty; a signature is not
                                        a `my` statement, so nothing is returned)
        PCL:  1 element

v1's signature lowering (`_sub_head`) models `sub foo ($x) {â¦}` as arity
checks plus a synthesized `my ($x) = @_;` STATEMENT.  With an empty body that
statement is the block's tail, so the sub returns the unpack's value.  Before
#721 that value was the RHS COUNT (1); after #721 it is the parameter ($x =
7).  Both are wrong -- perl returns ().

Reachable only when the body is EMPTY (or ends in the unpack itself), and
perl-tests/signatures.t's occurrences are subs that are only ever called for
their "Too few arguments" die, which is why no row moves.  A small file takes
a different lowering (`p-check-arity` + `let*` + an empty `(block nil)`) and
already answers () -- so the divergence is specific to the route that
synthesizes the `my` statement.

FIX SHAPE (not designed): the synthesized parameter binding is a BINDING, not
a statement value -- it should never be a block's tail form.  Either append an
explicit empty-list tail when the real body is empty, or mark the synthesized
statement so the tail machinery skips it.  Do NOT "fix" it by restoring the
scalar-context freeze: that is #721's bug and it is wrong for real `my`
declarations.

BAR: the row above vs perl for the package-block, glob-assigned and anon
spellings; a signature sub with a NON-empty body unchanged; signatures.t's
verdict unchanged; emission A/B over the four populations.
subject: an EMPTY-bodied signature sub returns its synthesized parameter unpack's value; perl returns ()
